newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares finish at fourth consecutive high. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 10/6]
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares finish at fourth consecutive high. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 10/6]

text.p: Dutch blue chips extended their bull-run on Monday to finish at their fourth consecutive all time high close after a day spent trading in record territory.
Late trades in index heavyweight ING, which were subsequently cancelled by the stock exchange, caused some confusion about the final level of the AEX.

For a period of some 90 minutes after close of trade, the closing level of the index fluctuated fractionally, with the listings officer restating the index twice before finally establishing the closing level at 829.43 points, a gain of 5.0 points on the day (corrects closing level).
The AEX index started the day at a record, shrugging off a slight softening in the dollar to focus on higher surrounding bourses and Wall Street's Friday climb.
It continued to trade above Friday's highest levels for the entire session, peaking at a new intra-day high of 834.43 and never dropping below 826.91 points.
After options-led offering pared gains at midsession, the market got a second wind in late trade on Wall Street's early surge and looked set to close a solid one percent up, just off the day's peak.

But the bond market's retreat on EMU jitters in the wake of France's request for more time to study stability pact proposals dragged shares down in the closing minutes, almost halving earlier gains to 0.61 percent.
A major contributor to the index rise was financial services group ING, adding 0.90 guilders to close at 90.10, off a high of 90.90.

Initially the stock had been thought to close up 1.10 guilders, but several after-the-bell trades were subsequently cancelled, a stock exchange spokesman said. Dealers said ING was catching up after lagging the earlier rise. Sector rival ABN Amro also profited from the upbeat sentiment, adding 0.50 guilders to 36.90 in brisk trade.
On the AMX midcap index, retail and services giant Vendex ended the session down 0.70 guilders at 109.20, after briefly hitting a low of 106.80 guilders.
Dealers said the fall reflected warnings from some analysts the share price might have risen too far.

In the past Vendex has been rated partly in line with the high price-earnings ratios afforded to stocks in the temporary employment services sector, but it recently spun off part of its Vedior temping arm as a separately listed company.
Vedior, by contrast, added 1.10 guilders to finish at 48.00, the same price at which it started trading last Thursday after its shares were issued at 39.00 guilders.
